list: The published PS5 list: 55 trophies in total — 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver and 46 bronze.
sources: Exophase trophy list for Grand Theft Auto VI (PSN): https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
PSNProfiles trophy page for Grand Theft Auto VI: https://psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi
PlayStation Network — the official names, descriptions and grades reproduced from PSN

roadmap.title: First hours — Chapter 1 at an easy pace
roadmap.text: Open the campaign and clear Chapter 1, including Gone Fishing and Breakfast Run. Two routines start now and pay rent for the entire run: save manually before every chapter ends, and feed the slow counters whenever the game offers a free chance — climb into cars you have never driven, take stunt jumps you roll past, and spend money in shops instead of hoarding it.

roadmap.title: Chapters 2–4 — story first, moments as they come
roadmap.text: Push the story through Chapters 2, 3 and 4 and the named missions The Cartel Heist, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory. Certain rooms and scenes may not stay reachable afterwards, so settle their one-off trophies on the spot: the unscheduled exit at VCIA, the cocktail on Ocean Beach, the loud way out of a showroom. Those moments are exactly why the missable flags exist.

roadmap.title: Strangers — close strands, do not collect them
roadmap.text: Pick up stranger strands as they surface and finish each one: the finales for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, the unique-animal hunt for Bret, and eight completed strands overall for the silver Strangers & Freaks. A strand only counts at its final mission, so one closed strand is worth more than three left dangling.

roadmap.title: Activities — taste everything, then chase scores
roadmap.text: Lap one: try each of the nine activity types once and bank Master of None. Lap two is the scored work: gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, a Top Fun drone win at each of the 14 locations, 20 wins across different races, a fishing victory over Cal, one arcade game played to its end, and the bowling follow-through at Kolt & Associates. Everything here repeats freely, so this stage costs hours, never trophies.

roadmap.title: The long haul — collectibles and the big counters
roadmap.text: The biggest single block of the platinum. Sweep Leonida district by district so the hunts overlap: meditate at all 18 spots, complete 3 Collectible Card sets, WAiNK It at 100 locations, discover 100 vehicles, open all 52 areas, finish 50 Challenges and land 250 stunts. Update the counters in this tracker as you travel — these trophies punish a late start, not a mistake.

roadmap.title: Crime, partners and the cash loop
roadmap.text: Armed with money and gear, clear the crime shelf: 5 Bank Vault robberies with clean escapes, an Armored Truck hit, one Illegal Operation from each of the 9 gangs, a jewelry store robbed without detection, and the partner pair — shaking a 4-star Wanted Level together and robbing 3 shops back-to-back together without the heat dying. Then shut the money loop: launder $250,000 of Marked Bills, spend $100,000 in shops, buy all 8 garage properties and register 10 vehicles on Scooter Bros.

roadmap.title: Endgame — cleanup, 100 percent, finale, platinum
roadmap.text: Filter this tracker down to whatever is left and sweep it. Missable flags first — if a moment slipped past, reload one of the rotating saves from Stages 1 and 2. Then the vague one-offs (the partnership moment, the fail-then-succeed moment, the strange event) and the push to 100 percent for A Long Road. Keep the final mission for last so the story trophies land together; Vice Got a Price! then follows on its own once the other 54 are in. The 90–130 hour total is an estimate reasoned from the official counts — 250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots, 42 range golds, 52 areas — not a promise.

Choose three nearby shops before starting, rob the first, and drive straight to the next without hiding long enough for your stars to clear. Planning that little circuit in advance is most of the work.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: MISSABLE, flagged openly: the official wording — a partnership with mass appeal — is deliberately vague and names no place, count or action, so no honest guide can hand you a verified step for it yet. What the list itself supports: it sits among the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy), so do partner activities thoroughly, take partner set-pieces when they are offered, and keep rotating saves through the story so a one-off partnership moment can be replayed. Nothing beyond what the description supports is claimed here.
steps: Do the other partner trophies properly
Say yes to partner set-pieces when offered
Keep rotating saves as the story advances
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Flagged missable-adjacent for a simple reason: its subject is choices, and no single playthrough lets you revisit every choice you made. The description itself says almost nothing — choices happen, for better or worse — but the list data attaches a PSN count of 500, so read it as a decisions-volume trophy. Choose deliberately whenever the game asks (dialogue picks, mission calls, world decisions) instead of drifting past on defaults, and measure yourself against the 500 target in the counter. If a branch ever seals content off, the rotating saves from Stage 1 are the fallback.
steps: Choose deliberately whenever the game asks
Measure progress against the 500 PSN target
Save before any branch that looks permanent
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. Read the wording literally: it rewards succeeding on a second attempt, which means a spotless first-try run can stroll straight past it. The working method follows from that shape — when something fails naturally, retry it on the spot rather than reloading to pretend the failure never happened, because fail-then-succeed is precisely the sequence being described. Still missing it near the end? Fail a repeatable attempt on purpose, then nail the retry. This stays labelled as a reading of the wording, not a confirmed trigger.
steps: Let natural failures stand — do not reload them away
Retry on the spot after failing
If all else fails: fail a repeatable try on purpose, then succeed
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: MISSABLE. The official wording has the classic shape of a strange, possibly random world event — something witnessed rather than scheduled. The practical advice that follows from that shape alone: explore on foot and at odd hours as well as by highway, avoid fast-travelling past the world, and when something odd starts happening, stay and watch it finish instead of driving on. No event, place or creature is invented here, because the official wording names none.
steps: See the world instead of fast-travelling past it
Stop for anything strange rather than driving on
Stay with the event until it ends
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a target down with a melee drive-by, per the official wording — striking from a moving vehicle with melee, not with the vehicle itself and not with a firearm. Set it up at low speed on a quiet street so the swing connects cleanly: roll past the target and strike as you pass. It repeats freely in free roam, so a miss costs only another pass.
steps: Set up a melee option usable from a vehicle
Roll past a target at low speed
Land the melee strike as you pass
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. It is a money-loop trophy with a big round target, so build the loop early — by Stage 6 at the latest — and route Marked Bills to contacts whenever they land in your hands instead of letting them sit. Track the laundered total in the counter so the closing stretch becomes a planned series of runs. It pairs naturally with Treat Yo Self: one healthy cash loop feeds laundering and spending at the same time.
steps: Find contacts who launder Marked Bills
Send Marked Bills their way whenever you hold them
Get the laundered total to $250,000
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. Cumulative is the key word in the official phrasing — no single heroic purchase is required. The easy route is to simply not hoard: from Stage 1 onward, buy the vehicles, clothes, services and upgrades you actually want, and this bronze usually completes by itself somewhere inside Stage 6's property buying.
steps: Spend normally in shops from early on
Avoid hoarding all cash until the end
Reach $100,000 total spent
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Own every garage property — eight of them in the official list data. Nothing here tests skill; it tests cash flow, so it waits on the money loop of robberies, laundering and story paydays. Schedule it for Stage 6 when income is steady, pick garages off one at a time as each becomes affordable, and log every purchase. As a bonus, owned garages give the vehicle habit behind Whip It Good somewhere to live.
steps: Get income steady first
Buy garages one by one as cash allows
End up owning all 8
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles on the Scooter Bros app. The trick is timing, not volume: register each keeper at the moment you acquire it — particularly the distinct vehicles you are already discovering for Whip It Good — instead of batching registrations later and losing track of which ones were never entered. With that habit in place, ten is a small number.
steps: Open Scooter Bros for each vehicle you keep
Register vehicles as they arrive, not later
Get the registered count to 10
trophies.sources: PlayStation's official list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guide text written for this entry.
